{"id": "80:1/q15", "question": "What was God teaching through the rebuke?", "turns_on": "Whether the rebuke chiefly teaches social and spiritual priority, refinement of the Prophet's visible conduct, limits on his missionary burden, or fuller assessment of benefits.", "positions": [{"id": "80:1/q15/p1", "position": "Give receptive, sincere believers priority and do not favor rank or wealth.", "reasons": "Zajjāj says not to neglect a Muslim for another; Jishumī says to uphold the guided believer and prevent alienation. Kashshāf reports Sufyān's poor-led gatherings as etiquette learned from this verse. Ibn Kathīr extends equal warning across status, gender, and age, since God guides whom He wills. Qurtubī and Study Quran compare 6:52 and 18:28; Study Quran cites 28:56 for the Prophet's limited power to guide. Ṭabāṭabāʾī contrasts rich and poor; Iṣlāḥī stresses willing companions over unresponsive chiefs."}, {"id": "80:1/q15/p2", "position": "The Prophet was being refined in manners, with the apparent class preference corrected.", "reasons": "Jishumī says the act must not become habitual; Ṭabrisī says it could wrongly imply poverty caused dismissal. Rāzī says the scene seemed to break poor believers' hearts and put worldly standing before religion, comparing 6:52. Ibn ʿĀshūr calls it a lapse in focus; Kur'an Yolu compares another prophetic correction at 9:43 and calls this tone especially stern."}, {"id": "80:1/q15/p3", "position": "The affectionate correction limits the Prophet's burden and indirectly rebukes the arrogant leaders.", "reasons": "Iṣlāḥī says the chiefs wanted poor companions excluded; he reads the apparent reproach as an indirect condemnation of them, using Farāhī's shepherd and lost sheep analogy. The Prophet's zeal led him to assume more responsibility than assigned; Iṣlāḥī compares Moses' eagerness at Ṭūr and 26:3."}, {"id": "80:1/q15/p4", "position": "The lesson is to weigh hidden benefits as well as obvious missionary gains.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr says the sūra teaches investigation of unseen factors and comparison of equal or greater benefits; he likens it to legal theorists requiring a mujtahid to seek conflicting evidence."}]}
{"id": "80:1/q16", "question": "Why is the visitor called blind in the following verse?", "turns_on": "Whether the physical description is a slight or a reason for greater care.", "positions": [{"id": "80:1/q16/p1", "position": "His blindness should have increased compassion and welcome, so naming it sharpens the reproach.", "reasons": "Kashshāf and Rāzī say the description is no insult; the condition creates a stronger claim to care."}, {"id": "80:1/q16/p2", "position": "Calling him blind seems degrading amid an otherwise honorific rebuke.", "reasons": "Rāzī raises this as an objection to the passage's description."}]}
{"id": "80:1/q17", "question": "What does this self-reproach show about revelation?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "80:1/q17/p1", "position": "The Prophet conveyed God's criticism of himself, showing faithful, objective transmission.", "reasons": "Ibn Zayd's saying in Thaʿlabī, Jishumī, and Durr says he would have concealed this passage if he concealed anything. Ibn ʿAṭiyya adds the Zayd and Zaynab verses. Asad links public transmission to 53:3. Kur'an Yolu sees sincerity, love of truth, and evidence that the Prophet conveyed God's word rather than his wishes; it also rejects treating him as incapable of error."}]}
{"id": "80:1/q18", "question": "What is this sūra called?", "turns_on": "The titles are drawn from the opening, distinctive later words, or the story's central person.", "positions": [{"id": "80:1/q18/p1", "position": "Its standard title is Sūrat ʿAbasa.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr says al-Suyūṭī's list omits alternative titles and lists it as ʿAbasa; Biqāʿī says this title points to the lesson and contrasts other names evoking the destructive blast."}, {"id": "80:1/q18/p2", "position": "It is also called al-Ṣākhkhah, al-Safarah, or al-Aʿmā.", "reasons": "Ālūsī reports these alternate titles. Ibn ʿĀshūr attributes al-Ṣākhkhah to Khafājī and al-Safarah or al-Aʿmā to ʿAynī; Study Quran locates their distinctive words in verses 33 and 15."}, {"id": "80:1/q18/p3", "position": "Ibn al-ʿArabī also called it Sūrat Ibn Umm Maktūm.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr says he found this title nowhere else."}]}
{"id": "80:1/q19", "question": "Where was this sūra revealed?", "turns_on": "Whether consensus on Meccan revelation resolves Ibn al-ʿArabī's broader chronological uncertainty.", "positions": [{"id": "80:1/q19/p1", "position": "It was revealed in Mecca.", "reasons": "Māwardī, Ālūsī, and Ibn ʿĀshūr claim agreement or consensus; Durr transmits Meccan reports from Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn al-Zubayr. Study Quran calls it early Makkan. Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects Ibn al-ʿArabī's uncertainty on this point."}, {"id": "80:1/q19/p2", "position": "The Meccan or Medinan classification and the date of Ibn Umm Maktūm's conversion were not established.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr reports Ibn al-ʿArabī's uncertainty but rejects it for this sūra because exegetes agree it is Meccan."}]}
{"id": "80:1/q20", "question": "How many verses are counted in this sūra?", "turns_on": "Regional verse counting yields 40, 41, or 42; Jishumī gives 45.", "positions": [{"id": "80:1/q20/p1", "position": "Forty-two verses.", "reasons": "Bayḍāwī and Durr state 42; Ālūsī and Ibn ʿĀshūr assign it to the Hijazi or Meccan, Kufan, and some Medinan counts."}, {"id": "80:1/q20/p2", "position": "Forty-one verses.", "reasons": "Bursevī lists it as one option; Ālūsī and Ibn ʿĀshūr attribute it to Basra."}, {"id": "80:1/q20/p3", "position": "Forty verses.", "reasons": "Bursevī lists it as one option; Ālūsī attributes it to the Syrian and first Medinan counts, and Ibn ʿĀshūr to Syria."}, {"id": "80:1/q20/p4", "position": "Forty-five verses.", "reasons": "Jishumī gives this count."}]}
{"id": "80:1/q21", "question": "Where does the sūra fall in revelation and Qurʾānic division?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "80:1/q21/p1", "position": "It is twenty-fourth in revelation, between al-Najm and al-Qadr, and begins the middle Mufaṣṣal.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr gives the revelation sequence and section placement."}]}
{"id": "80:1/q22", "question": "What virtue is reported for reciting the sūra?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "80:1/q22/p1", "position": "Its reciter will arrive on Resurrection Day with a smiling, delighted face.", "reasons": "Jishumī reports a transmission from Ubayy from the Prophet."}]}
{"id": "80:1/q23", "question": "May reciters add their own words to the sūra?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "80:1/q23/p1", "position": "No; the Prophet stopped additions and said the sūra's own wording was sufficient or complete.", "reasons": "Durr transmits Abū Wāʾil's account of a Banū Asad delegate adding a line about God creating a child, and Anas's account of al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Yazīd adding a line; the Prophet corrected each."}]}
{"id": "80:1/q24", "question": "How does the opening connect to the preceding sūra?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "80:1/q24/p1", "position": "It applies al-Nāziʿāt 79:45's warning to those who fear Judgment by distinguishing receptive seekers from indifferent leaders.", "reasons": "Jishumī and Ālūsī connect the closing warning to this opening; Biqāʿī extends the theme to resurrection, human creation, and food as proofs. Iṣlāḥī says the two sūras pair in theme, style, and reasoning, with different topic order; Study Quran reports the same link."}]}
{"id": "80:1/q25", "question": "How does this opening fit the rest of the sūra?", "turns_on": "Whether the intra-sūra link is the sustained contrast of receptive and resistant hearers or the repeated imagery of turning and flight.", "positions": [{"id": "80:1/q25/p1", "position": "The sūra contrasts resistant chiefs with believers seeking instruction, then expands to revelation, human dependence, and resurrection.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr describes praise of the Quran and its teaching, followed by Quraysh resistance that had occupied the Prophet. Ṭabāṭabāʾī traces poor versus wealthy, human ingratitude, and final recompense. Biqāʿī reads the basmala as God's universal creation and guidance and particular favor to allies; Ibn ʿĀshūr notes that his occasion discussion follows at 80:1."}, {"id": "80:1/q25/p2", "position": "The opening's turning away anticipates the later scene of people fleeing one another.", "reasons": "Sāmarrāʾī links turning away, inward flight in the frown, and distraction from the seeker with the flight scene at 80:34, also citing 80:10."}]}
{"id": "80:1/q26", "question": "What inward lesson is drawn from the opening?", "turns_on": "Whether the inward emphasis falls on a guide's treatment of seekers or the Prophet's divine education and relation to God.", "positions": [{"id": "80:1/q26/p1", "position": "A spiritual guide should judge readiness for faith rather than outward status and attend to a prepared weak seeker.", "reasons": "Qāshānī says wealthy appearance can veil inward readiness: the poor man may perfect himself and guide others, while the rich man may remain arrogant and unbelieving. Sulamī reports that the gentle rebuke honors poverty and the sincere poor."}, {"id": "80:1/q26/p2", "position": "The Prophet's self briefly veiled him from truth as God educated him toward spiritual steadiness.", "reasons": "Qāshānī cites 'My Lord disciplined me and perfected my discipline'; he describes adoption of divine qualities after arrival, annihilation, and abiding. Qushayrī says God's noble name opens generosity to believers while His mighty name eludes seekers, and that God is known and remembered only through Himself, beyond time and place."}]}

{"id": "80:3/q04", "question": "Does 'perhaps he may purify himself' complete the verb of knowing or begin independently?", "turns_on": "Whether laʿalla blocks the verb's government, an object is supplied by the following clause, or the object is omitted before a new sentence.", "positions": [{"id": "80:3/q04/p1", "position": "It supplies what the Prophet could not know: that the man might purify himself.", "reasons": "Al-Alusi calls this the apparent attachment of the clause to the knowing verb as its object and identifies the pronoun with the blind man."}, {"id": "80:3/q04/p2", "position": "Laʿalla suspends the knowing verb's object governance, making the following clause independent.", "reasons": "Al-Samin and Abu ʿAli al-Farisi, as reported by Ibn ʿAshur, liken hope to interrogation because both request; Ibn ʿAshur says causative yudrīka then retains one object rather than three. {"id": "80:3/q05", "question": "What force does 'perhaps' have here?", "turns_on": "Whether laʿalla is read as hope, an interrogative, or assurance in divine speech, and whose perspective supplies the hope.", "positions": [{"id": "80:3/q05/p1", "position": "It conveys a real prospect or hope, whether felt by the blind man or viewed from the Prophet's standpoint.", "reasons": "Al-Alusi says either person's hope is enough to forbid neglect, especially given the seeker's receptiveness. {"id": "80:3/q18", "question": "What teaching priority follows from the possible purification of the seeker?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "80:3/q18/p1", "position": "Attend to receptive seekers, even when their benefit is only hoped for; wealth or rank cannot replace willingness to learn.", "reasons": "Bursevi says outwardly preferring the rich hurt the poor seeker despite a hoped-for larger conversion benefit, so the better course was missed. {"id": "80:3/q19", "question": "How does this episode serve the sura's wider message?", "turns_on": "How the episode is related to the sura's themes and to al-Naziʿat.", "positions": [{"id": "80:3/q19/p1", "position": "It opens a rebuke of favoring privileged people over poor believers, followed by human dependence, ingratitude, resurrection, recompense and warning.", "reasons": "Tabatabaʾi traces that sequence through the sura."}, {"id": "80:3/q19/p2", "position": "It shows the warning mission purifying receptive hearts; creation and food then show God's power and the folly of rejection.", "reasons": "Al-Biqaʿi links warning those who fear, citing 79:45, to resurrection, human creation and sustenance."}, {"id": "80:3/q19/p3", "position": "It shares al-Naziʿat's central theme, discourse style and reasoning, while changing the order of topics.", "reasons": "Islahi describes the two suras as a pair and notes this sura's distinctive sequence; the note mentions 79:45."}]}
